root_cause.text: Using non-RCU-safe hlist_for_each_entry_safe() to iterate over RCU-protected hash buckets in dev_map_redirect_multi() and an incorrect lockdep condition in dev_map_enqueue_multi(), both missing the required acquire barrier and lockdep annotation for correct RCU traversal, leading to potential use-after-free or data races on weakly-ordered architectures.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces hlist_for_each_entry_safe() with hlist_for_each_entry_rcu() using rcu_read_lock_bh_held() as the lockdep condition, and fixes the lockdep condition in dev_map_enqueue_multi() from lockdep_is_held(&dtab->index_lock) to rcu_read_lock_bh_held(). The CVE description explicitly states that the original code "performs plain pointer dereferences without rcu_dereference(), missing the acquire barrier needed to pair with writers' rcu_assign_pointer()" and that this can cause readers to observe partially-constructed nodes on ARM64, POWER.
